heard: One supergiant galaxy almost bridges the Milky Way and Andromeda. On June 19, 1790, astronomer William Herschel discovered this faint celestial smudge in the constellation Virgo. Today, we know that smudge as IC-1101, anchored at the center of the Abel 2029 galaxy cluster. Recent ultra-deep observations using the Isaac-Newton telescope revealed its measured main body spans 1.7 million light years. Containing trillions of solar masses, this cosmic colossus grew into a monster by cannibalizing neighboring galaxies. Faint plume-like outer remnants show that it is still actively devouring nearby galactic debris today. That is why this supergiant galaxy is so massive it would almost bridge the Milky Way and Andromeda.
